paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD is the One who made everything, and He won't share that spot with anybody. Pharaoh stood by the Nile and said, "The Nile is mine; I made it myself." That's like a guy at work taking credit for the whole project because he sent one email. Everything we have, we got from God, so bragging on it is a bad trade (Ezekiel 29:3).

Now look at the staff of reeds. Israel leaned on Egypt, and it splintered and broke (Ezekiel 29:6-7). I know that feeling, baker. I once leaned on a cheap chair too, and I got a good look at the ceiling. When we trust something that was never strong enough to hold us, it gives out right when we need it. God keeps showing us that He is the One who can be leaned on.

And hear this part: God has the last word, and He keeps His promises. Egypt gets scattered and brought back, and Nebuchadnezzar gets paid for work that, God says, "was done for Me" (Ezekiel 29:20). Then God says He will cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel (Ezekiel 29:21). So ask yourself, baker, what are you leaning on today? Lean on the LORD, because nothing He holds up ever snaps.
